title: fix: correct burst accounting and utilization reporting in dedicated autoscaler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes incorrect burst token accounting and improves fleet utilization reporting; no user-facing config changes required.
commits: fix: normalize token units before bucket calculations
perf: avoid double-counting in in-flight request counter
test: add integration test for burst smoothing under synthetic load
telemetry: emit fleet-level burst_alloc and burst_used metrics
docs: add note about burst smoothing parameters
description: Context: customers reported intermittent spike throttling on Dedicated fleets when short bursts overlapped with autoscaler scale-up events. Root cause: tokenbucket smoothing logic used request counts in 'raw' units while utilization reporting pipeline expected normalized GPU_token units, leading to over-allocation of burst capacity and inflated fleet utilization metrics. This caused the autoscaler to throttle unnecessary requests during recovery window. Changes: 1) normalize all token math to GPU_token units via a new util/units.go helper and convert upstream inputs; 2) fix double-counting in manager.go by moving in-flight decrement into the single exit path and guarding against duplicate callbacks; 3) emit new telemetry metrics (fleet.burst_alloc, fleet.burst_used, fleet.token_unit) and add tags for fleet_id and region for easier aggregation; 4) add integration test simulating overlapping bursts and scale-up to prevent regressions; 5) update alert thresholds in observability/alerts.yaml to reduce noisy alerts until one stable window after deploy. Checklist: [x] unit tests updated; [x] integration test added; [x] telemetry/metric names reviewed; [x] changelog/release notes drafted; [x] Linear ticket(s) linked. Commits summary: 5 commits, small refactors and telemetry additions. Review highlights: - Diego: requested a nil guard in tokenbucket callback and argued for more explicit unit conversions in telemetry; author updated manager.go and added units.go with comments explaining conversions. - Priya: asked for a small performance microbenchmark for the refactor; author added a perf test in scripts/load-sim and posted results in review thread showing <2% overhead. - Liam: requested clearer metric naming and tag usage; metrics adapted and tests updated. CI: first run failed one flaky integration test (timeout), test timeout increased and test stabilized; subsequent CI run passed all checks (build, unit, integration, lint). Merge: approved by Diego and Priya, merged by squash on 2026-02-24. Impact: fixes incorrect utilization reporting and reduces spurious throttling during burst+scale events; customers on Dedicated fleets should see more stable throughput during recoveries. Rollout notes: deploy to canary Dedicated clusters first, monitor fleet.burst_used and fleet.burst_alloc for expected ratios, then rollout to all regions. Related: ENG-2178, SUP-4021.
